title: React Native and Vega OS integration
lead: Run the React Native sample in a generated Expo project, or build the included Vega Kepler app. Try their source, playback, subtitle, and UI settings and inspect the applied configuration code.

blocks.text: React Native and Expo

apps/react-native provides the existing showcase App.tsx, source list, DVR logic, configuration controls, and a generator for an external Expo development project. The generated host pins Node 24.19.0, pnpm 10.33.0, Expo 57.0.30, React Native 0.86.3, React 19.2.3, bitmovin-player-react-native 1.29.0, expo-crypto 57.0.4, and expo-clipboard 57.0.2. Its pnpm-lock.yaml preserves the JavaScript dependency resolution.

The wrapper resolves iOS Player and Player Core 3.128.0, Analytics 3.28.1, and Google IMA 3.26.1 through Swift Package Manager; Android Player is 3.170.0+jason. The included native dependency locks preserve the iOS resolution. The standalone samples have independent SDK pins. Keep the wrapper's supported native dependencies together rather than overriding them with the standalone Android 3.171.0 pin.

The +jason suffix selects Bitmovin's Android build that renames media-library namespaces and resources to avoid conflicts with Media3/ExoPlayer. Google IMA 3.37.0 and later require this build and core-library desugaring, which adapts newer Java library APIs for older Android versions. Wrapper 1.29.0 selects Player and media-session 3.170.0+jason, IMA 3.38.0, desugar_jdk_libs 2.1.5, and okhttp-urlconnection 5.5.0. Its Expo plugin has no native Player SDK version option. Keep these related dependencies together; changing only the Player version is not a verified wrapper upgrade.

blocks.title: Generate the external host from the repository root
blocks.text:
pnpm --filter @showcase/ui-shared build
bash scripts/sync-env.sh
node apps/react-native/scripts/create-expo-project.mjs ../player-lab-react-native --env-from apps/react-native/.env

The generator uses the native template included in Expo 57 rather than create-expo-app@latest. Its target must be a new directory outside the checkout. It copies the existing App and registers it as the root screen with a safe area. Native Player modules require a development build; Expo Go cannot run them.
The generated app is named Player Lab React Native and uses com.playerlab.reactnative for both iOS and Android. Its app.json registers the Player plugin and the included shared UI asset plugin:

blocks.title: Generated app identifiers and plugins

items: Configure the repository root keys and run the preparation commands above. --env-from explicitly copies the generated ignored apps/react-native/.env with mode 0600; omit it to generate a project without keys. Keys are never inserted into app.json.
Authorize com.playerlab.reactnative on the Player license being used. Optional Analytics has a separate license and authorization. Never commit .env or native build output.

Install the generated pinned dependencies and run Expo prebuild. For iOS, restore the supplied Podfile.lock before pod install, then the supplied workspace Package.resolved before building, using the commands below.

The included plugin copies shared JS/CSS into Android app/src/main/assets/webui and iOS Copy Bundle Resources. App.tsx resolves Android asset URLs and iOS main-bundle filenames directly; no placeholder delivery path remains.

After editing the shared UI, rebuild it, copy its JS/CSS into the external project assets/webui directory, rerun prebuild, and rebuild the native app. A Metro reload alone cannot update native resources.
Run the iOS or Android development build from the external project and check the actual SDK UI, advancing VOD, Apply/Reset, and background/foreground return.

blocks.text: The generator copies the selected environment file once. To refresh keys in an existing external host, run scripts/sync-env.sh again from the repository root, copy apps/react-native/.env into the external host as .env with mode 0600, and restart Metro. That generated file provides the EXPO_PUBLIC_ variable names used by the App.

On macOS, use Xcode and CocoaPods for iOS; wrapper 1.29 requires iOS 16.4 or later. Android requires Java 17 and the Android SDK/toolchain selected by Expo 57. The wrapper's Expo plugin raises compileSdk to at least 37 and the Kotlin Gradle plugin to at least 2.2.21. The supplied Podfile.lock was generated with CocoaPods 1.17.0. Since wrapper 1.27, iOS Player and Google IMA use Swift Package Manager, while the bridge and Expo use CocoaPods. Existing integrations should follow the official migration guide. Keep both Podfile.lock and the workspace Package.resolved; restore the supplied locks after generating a fresh project.

blocks.title: Install, prebuild, and restore iOS dependency locks
blocks.text:
cd ../player-lab-react-native
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm exec expo prebuild --no-install
cp native-locks/Podfile.lock ios/Podfile.lock
(cd ios && pod install)
mkdir -p ios/PlayerLabReactNative.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm
cp native-locks/Package.resolved ios/PlayerLabReactNative.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved

blocks.title: Choose the target command in the external Expo project
blocks.text:
pnpm exec expo run:ios
pnpm exec expo run:android

The screen includes Default, Sports, Live (DVR), and Cinema UI choices; source buttons; Live edge; −10/−30/−60-second controls; Allow DVR; state; an event log; and Show configuration. iOS starts with HLS and offers HLS/progressive MP4; DASH types and presets are hidden there. Android also offers DASH.

items: Select a VOD preset and start playback in the player UI. Open Show configuration and Show applied code, and keep the original values for comparison.

Keep the source URL, enter 5 for Start offset (seconds), select Start, and use Apply and recreate player. This editor recreates the player even for a source-only change. Start playback if Autoplay is off, check the initial timeline position and look for a fresh SourceLoaded event.

Reopen the form and compare the buffer or bitrate inputs below. The applied code changes only after a successful Apply. It shows the configuration submitted to the native SDK, while the actual picture and track menus show what the source can play.

Use Reset draft to discard edits. To undo an applied experiment, restore the recorded values and Apply again. Initial player values are Autoplay off, Mute on startup off, blank Forward buffer and blank Maximum bitrate. Selecting a catalog preset restores its source fields but retains player settings.

rows: Apply recreates the player. Compare bufferConfig.audioAndVideo.forwardDuration in applied code. This is a buffer target, not a promised startup delay. Empty input returns to the platform SDK default.

Apply recreates the player. Compare adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate in applied code and playback on a source with multiple bitrates. The input is bits per second, so enter the number without Mbps or commas.
Your HTTPS WebVTT URL; label Test captions; language en; Mark as default off

Apply, then select Test captions in the player's subtitle menu and play through a cue's time range. Mark as default supplies metadata rather than enabling the track. Use a WebVTT file timed to the selected media.

The UI switch recreates the player and reloads the applied source. Compare the controls and the UI configuration in Show applied code. A source preset button instead loads its source into the existing player immediately.

blocks.text: The React Native configuration form has no initial audio-language preference, HTTP retry editor or TweaksConfig panel. Use the player UI for the track controls it provides, and the API coverage reference to distinguish form fields, UI presets and code-only support.

Show configuration edits the required HTTP/HTTPS source URL, type, optional title/poster URL, start offset in seconds, and its Start/End/SDK default reference. Signed offsets are allowed: Start refers to the beginning of the media/DVR window, End to the end/live edge. The SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live. Blank title/poster/offset fields remove those optional values.

External subtitle settings include External WebVTT URL, Subtitle label, Subtitle language and Mark as default. Supply URL, label and an IETF language tag together; en-us becomes en-US. Blank URL removes the track and clears its metadata. Mark as default sets native track metadata; choose the track in the SDK subtitle menu to enable it. Apply, Reset draft and code export use the same validated applied configuration.

blocks.caption: React Native on iOS: external WebVTT subtitle settings before Apply.
React Native on Android: external WebVTT fields with Mark as default off.

blocks.title: Scrolling menus inside the Android player
blocks.text: The player menu and the surrounding settings form are separate scroll areas. Swipe inside the video menu to reach lower items; start a swipe outside the video to scroll the form. A parent scroll view can intercept a gesture intended for the embedded menu, so the app keeps player touches with the video until they end or are cancelled. Replacing the player also releases that touch ownership.

Autoplay and Mute on startup apply at player creation. Start offsets and buffer durations accept finite decimal seconds. Blank buffer keeps the SDK default (iOS 0, Android 50); iOS 0 lets the SDK choose a duration. This form requires a positive Android buffer target because zero is not its automatic setting. Maximum bitrate accepts whole bits per second: 1–2,147,483,647 on Android and 1–9,007,199,254,740,991 on iOS; blank means no cap. The native bridge converts bitrate to an integer, Android uses a signed 32-bit value, and JavaScript cannot represent integers above its safe limit exactly. Fractions and out-of-range values are rejected before recreation.

Apply and recreate player validates the whole draft, recreates the player, and reloads the selected source from its start offset. Playback position resets and playback starts according to Autoplay. The complete source, chosen UI, log, and Allow DVR setting are retained. Invalid or unchanged settings do not recreate the player. Reset draft only discards edits; it does not change playback. Preset source buttons still load immediately. Allow DVR remains an application helper rather than an editable SDK playback property.

To display an external subtitle in React Native, apply its URL, label, language, and default metadata, then select the track in the Player subtitle menu. Mark as default supplies metadata; it does not enable the track by itself. Use a source and WebVTT file whose cue times overlap.

blocks.caption: React Native on iOS: the selected external subtitle is drawn over the native video.
React Native on Android: the selected external subtitle over the native video.

blocks.text: Vega OS and Kepler

Vega OS is separate from Android-based Fire TV. The included apps/vega host connects the modular Web Player to W3C Media and retains the existing React Native/Kepler controls. It does not use the browser-based bitmovin-player-ui. The tested combination is Player 8.138.0-beta.28, React Native 0.72.0, React 18.2.0, Kepler 2.1.0+rn0.72.0 and W3C Media 2.3.2, with Vega SDK 0.24.12112 and Kepler CLI platform 0.22.14. The official Vega sample supports the beta.XX channel; the general Web stable release is not a supported substitute.
Player Lab Vega uses com.playerlab.vega and the com.playerlab.vega.main component. Authorize this identifier for the configured Player license before a licensed device run.

items: Install the official Vega SDK and documented prerequisites. Normal JavaScript installation, unit tests and type checks do not require the native SDK or a license.
Use the included application host. Generate its ignored runtime configuration from your local licenses before bundling.

For licensed playback, load the repository-root .env with scripts/env-lib.sh and rerun runtime:config before rebuilding. It copies only the Player and optional Analytics licenses; index.js installs them before evaluating App. Authorize com.playerlab.vega on the Player license. Keep generated configuration, bundles, packages and logs private.
Run build:vega through the Vega SDK environment. It creates JS/Hermes bundles and aarch64, armv7 and x86_64 Release packages. The generic workspace build does not run the native SDK.

Start a Vega Virtual Device or connect a compatible device, verify its OS/profile, select its serial explicitly and launch the matching package. Check changing video frames and advancing SDK position together; a CLI ready message alone does not prove that the OS or app booted.

blocks.title: Load local licenses and build
blocks.text:
source scripts/env-lib.sh
load_env_defaults .env
pnpm --filter @showcase/vega runtime:config
vega exec pnpm --filter @showcase/vega build:vega

blocks.title: Inspect and run on a Vega Virtual Device
blocks.text:
vega virtual-device start --timeout 120
vega exec vda devices -l
vega device info --device <VVD_SERIAL>
vega run-app apps/vega/build/aarch64-release/vega_aarch64.vpkg \
  com.playerlab.vega.main --deviceId <VVD_SERIAL>

The screen includes source selection, Live edge, −10/−30/−60-second controls, Allow DVR, state, logs, and Show configuration. Autoplay and mute are initially enabled. Allow DVR, Autoplay and Mute on startup are explicitly focusable and can be toggled with D-pad and Select (arrow keys and Enter on VVD). The screen does not provide dedicated play/pause buttons, audio/subtitle/quality selection, media-key shortcuts or DRM modules.

items: Select VOD HLS and wait for moving video and an advancing position value. Keep Autoplay enabled while comparing settings: this host has no separate Play button.

Open Show configuration, record the baseline values, enter 5 for Start offset (seconds), choose Start and use Apply and recreate player. Check the new source load and the position displayed below the video after playback starts.

Use the example buffer and bitrate values below, Apply, and compare Show applied code with the baseline. A source edit also recreates the player; it waits for the previous native player to release its resources.

To discard edits use Reset draft. To restore initial player settings, set Autoplay and Mute on startup on, clear both buffer fields and Maximum video bitrate, then Apply. Select the VOD preset again to restore source fields. If Autoplay was turned off, turn it on and Apply to start a fresh playback session.

rows: Apply recreates the player. Check buffer.video.forwardduration and buffer.audio.forwardduration in applied code. The fields are separate targets for media held ahead; they do not extend a live stream's retained history.
Apply recreates the player. Check adaptation.bitrates.maxSelectableVideoBitrate in applied code and use a multi-bitrate source for playback comparisons. The host has no manual quality selector.
Your HTTPS WebVTT URL; label Test captions; language en; Enable external subtitle on load on
Apply, then play through a cue's time range. Vega draws plain subtitle text over the native video. Unlike React Native, this setting enables the configured track without a subtitle menu.
Title: Player Lab VOD; your HTTPS poster URL, if needed
Check the values in applied source code. This host displays no artwork overlay, so storing a poster does not create a visible poster image.

blocks.text: Show configuration edits an HTTP/HTTPS source URL, HLS/DASH/progressive MP4 type, optional title/poster URL, signed start offset in seconds and Start/End/SDK default reference. Start means beginning of media/DVR window, End means end/live edge; the SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live. Blank title/poster/offset fields remove those optional values. The Kepler screen has no artwork overlay, so a poster value is stored with the source without adding a visible poster.

External subtitle settings include External WebVTT URL, Subtitle label, Subtitle language and Enable external subtitle on load. Supply URL, label and an IETF language tag together; en-us becomes en-US. Blank URL removes the track and clears its metadata. The public Subtitles and WebVTT parser modules deliver cue events to a native plain-text overlay, which clears on source/player retirement or background transition. HTML cue styling is not rendered. HTTPS delivery produced visible cues in the checked runtime; the same local HTTP fixture did not. Reset only restores the draft; Apply recreates through the existing release barrier, and code export contains applied values only.

blocks.caption: Vega: the native video with the external WebVTT cue drawn by the app.

blocks.text: Autoplay and Mute on startup apply at player creation. Separate audio/video forward buffer targets are in seconds; this form accepts positive values, and blank keeps the SDK default of 40 seconds per media type. Live windows can limit the effective buffer. Maximum video bitrate is a positive adaptation cap in bits per second; blank means no cap. Numbers must be finite decimals. Format, buffering and adaptation support still depends on the stream, engine and target device.

Apply and recreate player validates the draft, waits for the previous player to close, and reloads the selected source from its start offset. Playback position resets and playback starts according to Autoplay; the selected/custom source, log and Allow DVR setting are retained. Invalid or unchanged settings do not recreate the player. Reset draft only discards edits. Preset source buttons still load immediately. The HTML Player UI remains disabled on Vega; Allow DVR controls an application helper.

When the Vega app returns from the background, it creates a new playback session and reloads the retained source and applied settings. Playback restarts according to the configured start offset and Autoplay value. This does not restore an arbitrary previous playback position.

Before player construction, the runtime connects the published Amazon media/WebCrypto APIs, @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12 and base-64 1.0.0. PlayerConfig.network.requestApi is fixed to Fetch as required by the integration; it is a code setting, not a GUI selector. Other supplied network hooks remain. Native media and crypto implementations stay in their installed packages. The state line displays PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime() in seconds; live sources can use an absolute media timeline.

If the app reports that the previous native player could not be released, restart the app before trying again. Creating another player while the previous one still owns native resources can prevent playback. This safeguard stops replacement and keeps the diagnostic visible.
Applied configuration code

Both configuration panels provide Show applied code. The output uses the applied configuration, includes no draft edits, and uses a Player-key placeholder. React Native includes the selected shared UI and provides Copy code through the pinned Expo Clipboard module. A native development build must include that module. Vega displays the configuration for its existing native media host; this TV sample has no clipboard integration. Keep the Vega host’s media and surface lifecycle when reusing the settings.

blocks.caption: React Native on iOS: applied configuration code and the license-key placeholder.
Vega: remote-readable applied configuration code with a license-key placeholder.
